topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the learning outcomes regarding the hallmarks of cancer and their underlying genetic mechanisms.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in signaling cascades, including Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinase pathways, confer growth signal independence and resistance to growth-inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells evade terminal differentiation to sustain proliferation in hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family regulators.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and bypass of cellular senescence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells achieve indefinite replication through telomerase reactivation and overcome p53-dependent senescence and DNA damage arrest.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the metabolic alterations of cancer cells, including the Warburg effect, tissue-specific metabolic profiles, and Krebs cycle mutations producing oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the angiogenic switch and the balance of regulatory signals required to supply oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and metastatic colonization
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the metastatic cascade from local invasion and circulation to the seed-and-soil dynamics and genomic profiles of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Conclusion and final remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a summary of how hallmarks integrate in cancer progression and guidance on further reading.
